paper.title: Fast UCB-type algorithms for stochastic bandits with heavy and super heavy symmetric noise

settings.name_in_paper: Stochastic MAB with heavy / super-heavy symmetric noise (Assumption 1)
unmapped: Reward X = mu_i + xi with noise having a symmetric density
Noise only needs E|xi|^alpha <= sigma^alpha for some alpha > 0 (possibly alpha < 1, no mean of the noise required)
settings.definition_quote: For any arm $i$ ($i=1,\dots,K$) and any round $t$ ($t=1, \dots, T$), random reward $X_i^t = \mu_i + \xi_i^t$ and the probability density function $\rho_i^t$ of the noise $\xi_i^t$ satisfy ... $\rho(u) = \rho(-u)$ for any $u \in \R$  (symmetric noise), there are $\sigma > 0$ and $\alpha>0$, such that $\EE[|\xi_i^t|^{\alpha}] \leq \sigma^{\alpha}$ (heavy tail).

symbols.g_inv: inverse in k of the bounding function g(k, delta) of the inner first-order optimization algorithm

conditions: inner first-order algorithm is g(k,delta)-bounding for f_i(x)=(x-mu_i)^2/2

source.label: thm:FO_UCB
source.quote: The regret of the \algname{FO-UCB} with $g(k, \delta)$-bounded first-order algorithm for the MAB problem with $K$ arms, auxiliary functions $f_i(x) = \frac{1}{2}(x-\mu_i)^2$, period $T$, $\delta=\frac{1}{T^2}$ satisfies R_T \leq \sum_{i: \Delta_i>0} \Delta_i (g^{-1}(\frac{\Delta_i^2}{8}, \frac{1}{T^2}) + 2)

results.notes: Generic reduction bound. Appendix restatement (Theorem 11) uses delta=1/(T(T+1)) and +1 instead of +2.

symbols.g_inv: inverse in k of the bounding function g(k, delta) of the inner zero-order optimization algorithm

conditions: inner algorithm is g(k,delta)-bounding for f_i(x)=|x-mu_i|

source.label: thm:ZO_UCB
source.quote: The regret of the \algname{ZO-UCB} with $g(k, \delta)$-bounded first-order algorithm for the MAB problem with $K$ arms, auxiliary functions $f_i(x) = |x-\mu_i|$, period $T$, $\delta=\frac{1}{T^2}$ satisfies R_T = \sum_{i=1}^K \Delta_i ( g^{-1}(\frac{\Delta_i}{2}, \frac{1}{T^2} ) + 2)

results.notes: Paper writes '=' but proof gives an upper bound; recorded as upper bound. Appendix restatement (Theorem 12) uses delta=1/(T(T+1)) and +1.

symbols.C_sgd: constant from the clipped-SGD convergence theorem (C = 5400 sigma^2 in the proof)
symbols.R_0: bound R >= |x_0 - x^*| on initial distance of the estimate to the mean

conditions: Assumptions 5 and 6 hold for the gradient estimator
number of iterations sufficiently large (from Theorem 7)

source.label: thm:MAB_theorem
source.quote: The regret of the \algname{Clipped-SGD-UCB} for multi-armed bandit problem with $K$ arms, period $T$, $\gamma = ...$, $\lambda_k= ...$ and symmetric distribution of rewards satisfies: R_T \leq 4\log((T+1)TR^2)\sqrt{C \log(4T(T+1)^2)TK} +  \sum_i \Delta_i

results.notes: Abstract summarizes as O(log T sqrt(KT log T)). The K in the tuning formulas is the optimization iteration count, not number of arms. Constants C, R not fully specified.

symbols.C_sgd: constant from the clipped-SGD convergence theorem (C = 5400 sigma^2 in the proof)
symbols.R_0: bound R >= |x_0 - x^*| on initial distance of the estimate to the mean

conditions: Assumptions 5 and 6 hold for the gradient estimator
number of iterations sufficiently large (from Theorem 7)

cited_results.setting_description: Stochastic K-armed bandits with heavy-tailed rewards, E|X|^{1+alpha} <= sigma^{1+alpha}, alpha in (0,1]
